chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Zur'ah ibn Muhammad, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And before that they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieve.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Jews found in their Books that Muhammad's (peace be upon him and his family) emigration would be between Ayr and Uhud, so they went out seeking the place. They passed by a mountain called Hadaad, so they said,

Those who were at Tayma longed for some of their brothers. A Bedouin from Qays passed by them, so they hired him. He said to them, 'I will pass with you between Ayr and Uhud.' They said to him, 'When you pass by these two, let us know.' When he was in the middle of the land of Medina, he said to them, 'That is Ayr and this is Uhud.' So they descended from the backs of his camels and said, 'We have achieved our goal, so we have no need for your camels; go wherever you wish.'

And they wrote to their brothers who were at Fadak and Khaybar, 'We have found the place, so come to us.' They wrote back to them, 'We have settled in the houses and acquired wealth, and we are close to you. So when that happens, we will quickly come to you.'

So they acquired wealth in the land of Medina. When their wealth increased, it reached Tubba', so he attacked them. They fortified themselves against him, so he besieged them. They felt sympathy for the weak ones of Tubba's companions, so they threw dates and barley to them at night. When that reached Tubba', he felt sympathy for them and granted them amnesty, so they came down to him.

He said to them, 'I have grown fond of your land and do not see myself except as remaining in you.' They said to him, 'That is not for you, for it is the emigration of a Prophet, and it is not for anyone until that happens.' He said to them, 'I will leave behind among you members of my family, so when that happens, they will support him and help him.'

So he left behind two tribes, Al-Aws and Al-Khazraj. When they multiplied there, they used to take the wealth of the Jews. The Jews used to say to them, 'But if Muhammad is sent, he will surely drive you out from our houses and our wealth.'

So when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), the Helpers believed in him, but the Jews denied him. And this is the Statement of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And before that they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieve.'
When there came to them that which they did not recognize, they disbelieved in him. So the curse of Allah is on the disbelievers.

key_terms.يَسْتَفْتِحُونَ: They used to pray for victory

ai.seo_question: How did the Jews' knowledge of the Prophet's emigration location lead to their denial of him?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the historical context of the Quranic verse 'And before that, they used to pray for victory against those who disbelieved' (2:89), detailing how Jewish tribes identified the specific location of the Prophet's Hijra between Ayr and Uhud. It narrates the subsequent arrival of Tubba' and the establishment of the Aws and Khazraj tribes, who later became the Ansar, contrasting their acceptance of the Prophet with the Jews' denial upon his arrival. This narrative underscores the Shia scholarly view of 'Tahqiq al-Ma'rifah' (knowing the truth upon recognition) and the subsequent 'Kufr' (disbelief) of those who knew but rejected.
